allowed_dependency_manifest.content: For each fixed integer n greater than 1, consider the function E_n(x) = floor(n x) minus the sum over integers k with 1 <= k <= n of floor(k x) divided by k. The task is to determine the set of real x values for which E_n(x) attains its maximum over all real x, and to determine the corresponding maximal value M(n).

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer n with n > 1 and every integer a with 0 <= a <= n - 1, the real value E_n evaluated at (a divided by n) satisfies E_n(a/n) <= H_n minus 1; moreover, E_n(a/n) equals H_n minus 1 if and only if a equals n - 1.

payload.statement_nl: For every integer n>1 and every integer a with 0 <= a <= n-1, one has E_n(a/n) <= H_n - 1, and equality holds if and only if a = n-1.

equality_conditions: equality at the final bound forces d=1
equality in rearrangement then forces a=n-1
key_reductions: for a=db,n=dm the fractional parts repeat d times

result_payload.proof_nl:
Let H_n := \sum_{k=1}^n 1/k and write \{t\} for the fractional part of t. Fix n>1 and an integer a with 0\le a\le n-1.

If a=0, then E_n(0)=0<H_n-1, so the claim is immediate. Assume now a>0. Since a<n,
E_n(a/n)=\lfloor na/n\rfloor-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\lfloor ka/n\rfloor}{k}
= a-\sum_{k=1}^n \frac{ka/n-\{ka/n\}}{k}
= \sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\{ka/n\}}{k},
because \sum_{k=1}^n (ka/n)/k = a.

Set d=\gcd(a,n) and m=n/d. Write a=db with \gcd(b,m)=1. For k=jm+r with 0\le j\le d-1 and 1\le r\le m, we have
\{ka/n\}=\{(jm+r)b/m\}=\{rb/m\},
since jb is an integer. As r runs from 1 to m, the values \{rb/m\} are a permutation of
0,1/m,2/m,\dots,(m-1)/m,
because multiplication by b permutes the residue classes mod m. Hence the multiset of the n numbers \{ka/n\} (k=1,\dots,n) consists of d copies of each of these m values.

Now the weights 1,1/2,\dots,1/n are strictly decreasing, so by the rearrangement inequality the sum \sum_{k=1}^n \{ka/n\}/k is at most the same weights paired with the fractional parts in nonincreasing order. Denote this decreasing rearrangement by c_1\ge c_2\ge\cdots\ge c_n. Then
E_n(a/n)\le \sum_{k=1}^n \frac{c_k}{k}.

The rearranged sequence is explicit: for s=1,\dots,m-1, the value (m-s)/m occurs exactly d times, and 0 occurs exactly d times. Thus for k=(s-1)d+t with 1\le t\le d,
 c_k=\frac{m-s}{m}.
But
\frac{n-k}{n}=\frac{dm-(s-1)d-t}{dm}=\frac{m-s}{m}+\frac{d-t}{dm}\ge \frac{m-s}{m}=c_k.
Therefore c_k\le (n-k)/n for every k, and so
E_n(a/n)\le \sum_{k=1}^n \frac{n-k}{nk}
=\sum_{k=1}^{n-1}\left(\frac1k-\frac1n\right)
=H_{n-1}-\frac{n-1}{n}
=H_n-1.
This proves the inequality.

For equality, first note that if d>1 then already c_1=(m-1)/m<(n-1)/n, so the comparison c_k\le (n-k)/n is strict at k=1; hence equality is impossible. Thus equality forces d=1, i.e. \gcd(a,n)=1.

When d=1, the multiset of fractional parts is exactly \{0,1/n,\dots,(n-1)/n\}, and the rearrangement inequality is sharp only when the sequence \{a/n\},\{2a/n\},\dots,\{na/n\} is itself nonincreasing. Since its first term is \{a/n\}=a/n, the first term must be the largest value (n-1)/n. Hence a=n-1.

Conversely, if a=n-1 then \{ka/n\}=(n-k)/n for 1\le k\le n-1 and \{na/n\}=0, so
E_n((n-1)/n)=\sum_{k=1}^{n-1} \frac{n-k}{nk}=H_n-1.

Therefore E_n(a/n)\le H_n-1 for all integers 0\le a\le n-1, with equality iff a=n-1.
result_payload.proof_summary: Rewrite E_n(a/n) as a weighted sum of fractional parts, use the multiset structure of \{ka/n\} when a/n is reduced, apply rearrangement to maximize against decreasing weights 1/k, then compare the sorted fractional-part sequence termwise with (n-k)/n. Equality is forced only at a=n-1.

used_external_facts: Rearrangement inequality for a decreasing weight sequence.
